first.rationale: Competitor entry pricing creates an immediate, segment-specific acquisition risk among price-sensitive SMBs, and the inherited record indicates targeted promotional pricing previously lifted both acquisition and revenue in that segment. A small, guarded test is warranted because discounting can reduce long-term value or attract lower-quality accounts. Onboarding is also a plausible contributor to qualified revenue given the completion decline, so its prior evidence should be verified alongside pricing before final commitment.

mid.rationale: Run the shortened-onboarding experiment. It directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and is supported by verified evidence of higher completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (-2.1 days), and improved 30-day retention (+3%), making it the strongest sustainable qualified-revenue choice. Promotional pricing is rejected because its verified revenue lift came with materially worse 30-day retention (-12%).

final2.rationale: Continue with shortened onboarding. The deeper competitor cut increases urgency, but the only verified pricing evidence shows a 40% SMB discount produced 30-day retention down 12% and was explicitly judged unsustainable. Shortened onboarding directly addresses the current completion decline and previously improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than a retention-damaging price response.
